title: Workload-aware batching defaults (beta) — Release notes
author: Aditya Rao
body:
## Summary
We are launching a **beta** for *workload-aware batching defaults* (aka **tiered batching profiles**) to reduce per-token cost while preserving predictable tail latency. The feature introduces three SLO-oriented batching tiers:
- **fast**: minimize queueing and protect streaming cadence
- **standard**: balanced defaults for most interactive workloads
- **cost_efficient**: maximize throughput/efficiency with stronger overload guardrails

This beta ships in **Runtime 1.21** and is available across Hosted API, Dedicated, and Private deployments (with rollout controls).

## What’s new
### 1) Batching tier selection
A new config field is available on supported routes:
- `batching_tier: fast | standard | cost_efficient`

If a tier is set, Redwood computes safe defaults for batching/scheduling knobs (e.g., max batch size, max queue delay, decode prioritization) based on:
- workload signals (prompt length buckets, concurrency)
- streaming vs non-streaming
- model family and (where applicable) GPU SKU overrides

### 2) Safe-by-default guardrails + rollout controls
This beta is shipped behind a feature flag with staged enablement by model/region. It includes:
- overload protection alignment for cost_efficient tier (backpressure + load-shedding reason codes)
- canary + auto-rollback hooks driven by latency and error-rate signals

### 3) New observability for queueing and batch formation
Additional metrics and Console views are available to validate that the tier behaves as expected (see **Telemetry & validation** below).

## Availability
### Deployment modes
- **Hosted API:** available in beta via feature flag + allowlist (see Opt-in)
- **Dedicated:** available via per-deployment config once allowlisted; recommended to start with canary pools
- **Private (VPC / on-prem):** available starting with Runtime 1.21 charts/installer; flag must be enabled explicitly

### Supported routes (beta)
- Chat/Completions (streaming and non-streaming)
- Embeddings: *supported for telemetry and limited batching defaults*; tier impact is smaller and may be model-dependent

### Supported models (beta cohort)
Supported model IDs in the beta cohort (subject to expand during Phase 3/4):
- `rw-llama-3.1-8b-instruct`
- `rw-llama-3.1-70b-instruct`
- `rw-mistral-large-2`
- `rw-qwen2.5-32b-instruct`

Notes:
- Quantized variants may have separate defaults; if you are pinned to a quantized model, confirm allowlist coverage with your Solutions Engineer.
- Long-context variants have stricter guardrails; see Known limitations.

### Supported regions (Hosted beta)
- `us-east-1`
- `us-west-2`
- `eu-west-1`

Dedicated/Private: region availability depends on your deployment footprint; the tier logic is runtime-local.

## Feature flag
### Flag name
- Control plane flag: `tiered_batching_defaults_beta`

### Behavior when flag is OFF
- No tier defaults are applied implicitly.
- Any **explicit** batching knobs you already set continue to function as before.

### Behavior when flag is ON
- Tier selection is accepted and applied.
- (Hosted beta only) For allowlisted models/regions, **standard** may be set as the default tier for select traffic when `batching_tier` is unspecified. This is controlled via rollout percentage and can be disabled per customer on request.

## Tier definitions (customer-facing)
The tiers are intended to be *predictable presets*, not per-customer bespoke tuning.

| Tier | Intended use | Primary objective | Expected trade-off |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `fast` | Latency-sensitive interactive chat, streaming UX, voice/agent loops | Lowest queue delay + steady token cadence | Higher $/1M tokens vs other tiers |
| `standard` | Default for most product chat and internal tools | Balance p95 latency and efficiency | Moderate batching; may increase latency slightly vs fast |
| `cost_efficient` | Offline-ish workloads, batch jobs, background tasks, high concurrency | Lowest $/1M tokens via higher batching | Higher queue delay and higher tail latency risk under bursty loads |

For exact SLO targets and measurement windows, see: **eng-sre/slo-and-error-budgets/latency-slo-tiers-fast-standard-costefficient**.

## How to opt in / opt out
### Hosted API (self-serve request-level opt-in)
You can opt in per request by providing `batching_tier`.

**Example (Chat Completions):**
- Request field: `batching_tier: "standard"`

If you are using an SDK, update to the newest beta-compatible version and pass `batching_tier` in the request options.

**Opt out:**
- Remove `batching_tier` from the request and/or set explicit batching knobs (if you already manage those).
- If your account is part of a default-on rollout (limited beta), Support can disable default-on behavior at the account level.

### Dedicated (per-deployment default)
- Set `batching_tier` on the route/model policy in your deployment config.
- Recommended rollout: start with `standard` on a canary pool, then expand.

**Opt out:**
- Remove `batching_tier` or revert to prior explicit knobs.
- Disable the flag `tiered_batching_defaults_beta` at the deployment level.

### Private (Helm / installer)
- Upgrade to Runtime 1.21 (or newer) and enable `tiered_batching_defaults_beta`.
- Set `batching_tier` in values for each route you want governed by tier defaults.

**Opt out:**
- Disable the flag and redeploy.
- Roll back to previous chart/runtime version if needed (see Known limitations and Rollback signals).

## Precedence rules (important)
Tiered defaults are designed to be non-breaking.

1) **Explicit batching configuration wins.** If you set specific knobs (e.g., max batch size, max queue delay), those values take precedence over tier defaults.
2) **Tier defaults apply next.** If `batching_tier` is set and knobs are not explicitly set, Redwood computes defaults.
3) **System defaults apply last.** If neither explicit knobs nor `batching_tier` are set, the runtime uses existing baseline defaults (unless you are in a Hosted default-on cohort).

## Telemetry & validation (what to look at)
### Console dashboards (recommended)
For allowlisted beta users, Console includes a "Batching tier" dashboard section with:
- p50/p95/p99 end-to-end latency by route/model/region
- queue delay histograms and percentiles
- batch size distribution (prefill and decode)
- GPU utilization and memory pressure (KV cache pressure signals)
- timeout and cancellation rates
- load-shedding counters with reason codes (primarily relevant for cost_efficient)

Dashboards spec reference: **eng-platform/dashboards-and-alerts/tiered-batching-observability-dashboards**.

### Request-level verification
To confirm what was applied, use one of the following:
- **Console → Route config → Effective configuration** (shows the resolved tier + overrides)
- **Config explain endpoint** (if enabled for your org): returns the effective config after precedence rules

If you are debugging, Support can enable temporary debug headers in staging to include:
- effective tier
- queue delay sample
- batch formation stats

### Key metrics to validate tier behavior
When comparing tiers, we recommend tracking at minimum:
- End-to-end latency: `latency_ms{p50,p95,p99}`
- Queue delay: `queue_delay_ms{p95,p99}`
- Batch formation: `batch_size` distribution + `batch_wait_ms`
- Throughput: tokens/sec (and requests/sec)
- Error rate: timeouts, cancellations, and load-shed events
- Streaming cadence (streaming routes): time-to-first-token and inter-token gap

## Known limitations (beta)
1) **Streaming sensitivity:** `fast` is tuned to protect cadence, but some workloads may still see increased inter-token gaps under bursty concurrency. If cadence is critical, start with `fast` and monitor cadence metrics.
2) **Long-context prompts:** prompts > ~16k tokens can shift the optimal prefill/decode balance. For long-context routes, expect tier impact to be smaller and guardrails to be more conservative.
3) **Tool/function calling workloads:** mixed tool-call patterns can create highly variable decode lengths; cost_efficient may increase queue delay variance.
4) **Highly spiky traffic:** cost_efficient assumes some concurrency stability. If your workload is spiky, the queue delay component can amplify tail latency. Consider `standard` + explicit admission control limits.
5) **Embeddings:** tiered batching is supported but not the primary focus of this beta; defaults may change as we expand the corpus and benchmarking.
6) **Cross-model routing:** if you use automated fallback across model variants, note that different models may have different tier defaults. Validate per-model behavior.

## Rollout guidance (beta best practices)
- Start with **standard** on one route, one model, one region.
- Ramp by percentage, not by flipping everything at once.
- Compare `standard` vs your current explicit/default behavior for 24–72 hours before trying cost_efficient.
- For cost_efficient, ensure overload protection is enabled and confirm your timeout settings are appropriate for added queue delay.

## Auto-rollback and “stop” signals (what triggers a pause)
During beta, Redwood will pause or roll back enablement for a cohort if any of the following are sustained beyond the configured window:
- p95 latency regression above tier thresholds (route/model/region)
- increased timeout or cancellation rates
- load-shedding events exceeding expected baseline for the workload
- streaming cadence regression (fast tier) confirmed by canary

## Customer comms / support
If you hit issues during beta, include the following in your ticket:
- model ID + region
- tier used
- streaming vs non-streaming
- approximate prompt length distribution and concurrency
- request timeout settings
- timeframe and request IDs (if available)

Support can assist with:
- confirming effective config (tier vs explicit overrides)
- recommending a tier per route
- enabling additional telemetry for short-term debugging

## Changelog (beta)
- Added `batching_tier` configuration (`fast`, `standard`, `cost_efficient`).
- Implemented tier-to-parameter mapping in the scheduler behind `tiered_batching_defaults_beta`.
- Added queue delay + batch formation metrics and tracing hooks for tail-latency debugging.
- Added overload protection alignment for cost_efficient tier.
- Added “effective config” explainability surfaces for debugging and Console display.

## Next steps
- Expand model and region coverage as perf canary results and customer feedback confirm stability.
- Tune tier defaults by model family and GPU SKU (where needed).
- Improve embeddings tier impact and documentation.

For roadmap and detailed tier definitions, see the PRD and design spec linked above.
